spike_verdict: n/a (spoke). Core hours, season, swim-section and water-quality claims stay within the sheet; five wording problems need repair.

blocking.claim: The fare was set to rise to $3 in January 2026. ... Our sources are reports of the plan, not a 2026 confirmation.
blocking.problem: Stale framing relative to 2026-10-13. The $3 base fare is confirmed live on the MTA site, but the page tells a visitor it is only a plan. Resolves sheet dead_end 'Whether the Jan 2026 fare and $35 cap actually took effect'.
blocking.evidence: https://www.mta.info/fares-tolls (fetched 2026-10-13): 'The fare is $3 for most riders on subways and local, limited, rush, and Select Bus Service buses.' and 'Reduced fares for seniors and people with qualifying disabilities are half the regular fare.' Sheet G24, G28.
blocking.fix: Replace the two fare paragraphs (from 'The fare was set to rise' through 'use a trip planner.') with: 'The subway and local bus fare is $3, according to the MTA's fares page in October 2026. The reduced fare is half of that, $1.50. The weekly fare cap is less clear. In September 2025, CBS New York reported a $35 cap for seven days of subway and bus rides. ABC7 had reported $36 in July 2025. The MTA fares page does not list the cap, so check the MTA before you count on either number. Our sources give no travel time from Midtown, so use a trip planner.' Add to sources: {"label":"MTA - Fares and tolls (checked October 2026)","url":"https://www.mta.info/fares-tolls"}.

blocking.claim: Fox 5 NY reported in May 2025, citing NYC Parks, that alcohol and dogs other than service animals are not allowed on New York City's public beaches.
blocking.problem: Picks one side of a listed conflict without saying sources differ. Sheet conflict [gaps] 'Dogs on city beaches': Fox 5 (G17) says dogs not permitted on beaches generally, but the Orchard Beach rules page (G14) bans dogs only from Memorial Day weekend to Oct. 1. Dead_end: no Coney Island alcohol or dog rule in any source. G17 is medium confidence. A visitor could be misled on dogs in the off-season.
blocking.evidence: G17 quote: 'alcoholic beverages and dogs, barring service animals, are not permitted on the beaches.' G14 quote: 'dogs, except service animals, on beach and promenade from memorial day weekend to oct. 1'.
blocking.fix: Replace the whole paragraph with: 'We found no alcohol or dog rule written for Coney Island Beach. Fox 5 NY reported in May 2025 that alcohol and dogs other than service animals are not permitted on the city's public beaches. That is a press summary for all eight city beaches. NYC Parks' own page for a different beach, Orchard Beach in the Bronx, bans dogs only from Memorial Day weekend to October 1, so the dog rule may depend on the season. Our sources say nothing about glass, grills or smoking at Coney Island. Before you bring alcohol, a dog or any of those, call 311 or the Parks beach office listed above.'

blocking.claim: The recent deaths on record here happened in water closed to swimmers.
blocking.problem: Overgeneralizes a safety statistic. The sheet holds exactly two incidents (July 2023, July 2024); dead_end says 'Any 2025 drownings or rescues at Coney; only 2023 and 2024 incidents'. 'Deaths on record' implies a full record.
blocking.evidence: V061, V062, V067, V068; dead_end [visit] drownings.
blocking.fix: Replace with: 'Two deaths described in our sources happened in water where swimming was not allowed.'

blocking.evidence: https://nyaquarium.com/about fetched 2026-10-13: animal chats, Sea of Illusions, Pumpkin Sculptures, Bubble Performances 'all included with admission'; no hours or dates.
blocking.fix: Replace with: 'The New York Aquarium's website promotes Ascarium events in October 2026, with animal chats, pumpkin sculptures and bubble shows included with admission. Our sources do not give its fall hours, so check nyaquarium.com before you go.'

advisory.claim: In 2026, Brooklyn's beaches opened on Saturday, May 23 ... Lifeguards sat in their chairs every day until September 13.
advisory.problem: V027/V028 are a May 21 preview ('will officially reopen', 'will be in their chairs'); page states it as held. Parks' Sept 2026 page (V008) supports the season window, but no source rules out early closures.
advisory.fix: Use: 'In 2026, Brooklyn's beaches were set to open on Saturday, May 23, at 10 a.m. Parks said the season ran through September 13, a week after Labor Day, with lifeguards on duty from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.'

advisory.claim: The beach is busy at night, but night swimming is not allowed. ... Coney Island is the only city beach where Parks runs a 24-hour operation.
advisory.problem: 'Busy at night' is in no fact. V035 quote is 'the only place where we have a 24 hour operation', not 'only city beach'.
advisory.fix: Write: 'Night swimming is not allowed. In May 2026, Parks Commissioner Tricia Shimamura said Coney Island is the only place where Parks runs a 24-hour operation. Swimming is still prohibited whenever lifeguards are off duty.'

advisory.claim: Officials give one main rule ... Gothamist said that was the most important warning from experts.
advisory.fix: Change 'Officials give one main rule' to 'Experts give one main rule'.
